guarantees.claim: The message FIFO write valid (wvalid_i) is gated by sha_en, so writes only occur when sha_en is asserted.
The clear input (clr_i) of u_msg_fifo is permanently tied to 0, preventing any software- or hardware-initiated FIFO clear.
The read valid input (rvalid_i) of u_tlul_adapter is tied to 1'b0, making all TL-UL reads invalid and (with ErrOnRead=1) guaranteeing an error response.

assumptions.claim: sha_en must be asserted only when the SHA engine is ready to accept message data; otherwise, the FIFO could accept writes at unintended times.
assumptions.cond: during normal operation when SHA is not ready
assumptions.risk: spurious or premature data may be written into the message FIFO, corrupting the hash computation.

assumptions.claim: The TL-UL bus (tl_win_h2d) must never issue a read request to this window because rvalid_i=0 will cause an error response (ErrOnRead=1).
assumptions.cond: if a read transaction is initiated
assumptions.risk: a bus error will be asserted on tl_win_d2h, potentially causing a fault or denial-of-service.

uncertain_points.claim: The error output (err_o) of u_msg_fifo is left unconnected. Any FIFO error (e.g., overflow) cannot be detected or handled.
uncertain_points.cond: whenever a FIFO error condition occurs
uncertain_points.risk: data corruption inside the HMAC message path may go undetected, compromising integrity of the hash computation.

uncertain_points.claim: The integrity error output (intg_error_o) of u_tlul_adapter is left unconnected. TL-UL integrity errors are not monitored or handled.
uncertain_points.cond: when a TL-UL integrity error is detected by the adapter
uncertain_points.risk: corrupted data from the bus could be written into the message FIFO without detection, undermining HMAC data integrity.
